post.summary: Starts a bulk add: creates a batch and a presigned PUT for the photo of several garments.
Checks the uploaded photo and starts the analysis; the app then polls GET /bulk/{id}.

get.summary: The status of a bulk add: everything the review screen draws.
get.description: Poll while status is Processing. Ready carries the pieces with private presigned links (thumbUrl for the grid, imageUrl for the review image) that expire at urlsExpireAt: ask again to refresh them. A likelyDuplicate is a hint about the caller's own wardrobe, never a block. Every sentence is the server's.

delete.summary: Cancels a bulk add: the pieces and every staged image are deleted. Idempotent.
delete.description: A cancelled or expired batch answers 204 again; a confirmed one 409 BulkAlreadyConfirmed.

post.summary: Adds the ticked pieces to the wardrobe; the pieces not listed are dropped with the batch.
post.description: Each listed piece becomes an ordinary wardrobe item whose id is the piece's id. A second confirm of the same batch answers 200 with the stored result and ignores the new body. 409 BulkNotReady before Ready, BulkExpired after a cancel or expiry; 503 StorageUnavailable commits nothing and is safe to retry.

put.description: Confirms the post's tags, caption and visibility. Visibility: Private (only the author), Followers or Public (everyone, signed out included). Followers is NOT a privacy boundary: following needs no approval, so any signed-in user can follow the author and then see the post; blocking someone removes their follow. Word the option accordingly in the app.

get.description: "Manken üstünde gör": the outfit drawn on a mannequin proportioned from the caller's measurements. Ready carries a presigned image URL (one hour); Preparing means a garment is still being prepared (ask again); Unavailable means the action must be hidden. A render reveals body proportions: the image is private to the caller. With check=true nothing is drawn and no render limit is spent: the answer is the status and reason only (Ready means a real request would draw it; imageUrl, garments and renderer stay empty), the way to decide whether to show the action. Ready carries renderer, which the app sends back with a "Yanlış görünüyor" report.

post.description: "Yanlış görünüyor": a mannequin drawing looks wrong. It must be about one of the caller's own drawings of that outfit or product, by the renderer the Ready answer named (else 404 TryOn.RenderNotFound). Stored for review (a garment shown from the back, most often); one report per drawing, the same drawing again stores nothing.

AcceptConsentRequest.description: The version the user saw and accepted; only the current one is accepted.

AccountAccessResponse.description: What disabling or enabling did. `RevokedTokens` is how many refresh tokens this call ended (0 when enabling).

AnonymousBudgetOutfitsRequest.description:
The acquisition variant: no wardrobe, no sizes, no persona, nothing stored. `Audience` (Women, Men or Unisex) is required; the rest, `IncludeShoes`
included, is as in `POST /me/outfits/budget`.

AnswerSizePromptRequest.description: `Size` is required for `BoughtFits`; for "too small" and "too large" it is the size that was bought, when the user says.

AnswerSizePromptResponse.description: `SizeEntry` is the user's entry for the brand and group after the answer (null when there is none).

AuthTokensResponse.description:
What every sign-in returns. `IsNewUser` is true only when this request created the account (register, or a first Google/Apple
sign-in); the app routes those users to onboarding.

BudgetOfferResponse.description:
The offer a bought piece comes from. `Price` includes shipping (`ShippingCost`, 0 when free: the app says "kargo dahil"); `OriginalPrice`
is the seller's crossed-out price on the same basis (list price plus the same shipping), present only with a real saving.

BudgetOutfitResponse.description:
A budget outfit. `Id` and `Status` exist for a signed-in caller (the outfit is stored: save, worn, feedback and dismiss work on it).
`Savings` appears only when a seller shows a real crossed-out price; `OverBudgetBy` only on the one over-budget answer.

BudgetOutfitsRequest.description:
`Budget` in TRY (100-100,000). `Occasion`: office, weekend, evening, sport or event. `Date`: today (default), tomorrow or
`yyyy-MM-dd` up to a week ahead. `UseWardrobe` (default true): owned pieces cost nothing and come first. `Seed` (default 0): the next
seed shows other outfits. `Count` 1-5 (default 3). `PersonaId` follows the catalog convention.
`IncludeShoes` (default true): false ("Ayakkabım var") builds outfits without shoes.

BudgetOutfitsResponse.description:
`Outfits` fit `Budget`. `WithoutShoes`: they have no shoes (the request said `includeShoes: false`, or no outfit with shoes fit and
`Message` says so). When nothing fits at all, `OverBudget` is true and the single outfit is the closest one (`Message` says by how
much), or the list is empty and `Message` says so. `Weather` is the forecast used, if any (signed-in callers with a city).

BudgetPieceResponse.description:
One piece. A wardrobe piece costs 0 and has `WardrobeItemId`; a catalog piece has `ProductId`, its `Offer` (the cheapest in the caller's
size, or the cheapest at all with `SizeUnknown`) and, when the size is known, `Size`.

BulkBatchResponse.description:
Everything the review screen draws (design note, section d); the app polls it every second or so while `Processing` and again to
refresh expired links. `Pieces` is empty unless `Ready`; `Items` is there only once `Confirmed`. Every sentence is the
server's (BulkAddCopy).

BulkBox.description: A box on the photo in fractions (0-1) of its width and height: left, top, width, height.

BulkConfirmPiece.description:
One ticked piece and its edits: `PATCH /items/{id}`'s own fields and rules for the category and the colours (a null field is left as the
analysis said, `clear: ["secondaryColor"]` empties the second colour). Everything else is edited afterwards with `PATCH`.

BulkConfirmRequest.description: The ticks are the list: a piece not in it is not added, and is gone with the batch.

BulkCreateUploadUrlResponse.description: PUT the photo to `UploadUrl` with exactly `Headers` before `ExpiresAt`, then call `process` on the batch.

BulkCutOff.description: Pieces the service found beyond what one batch keeps: how many, and the server's sentence (it names no limit).

BulkFailure.description: `Code` is the BulkFailureCode name; `Retryable` says whether "tekrar dene" (`process` again) makes sense.

BulkLikelyDuplicate.description: "Dolabında benzeri var.": the user's own item this piece looks like, with its normal public thumbnail. A hint, never a block.

BulkPieceResponse.description:
One piece of the review screen. `ThumbUrl` is the grid image (vision's 400 px thumbnail) and `ImageUrl` the review image (the cut-out as
vision sent it); both are private presigned links that expire at `UrlsExpireAt` (the app asks again). `Category`, the colours, the
pattern and `NeedsCategory` are the wardrobe item's own names and rules, so the single add's chips and pickers work unchanged.

BulkReason.description: Why a piece is not pre-ticked: the service's code and the server's sentence (BulkAddCopy).

BulkUnseparated.description: Garments the service saw together and could not cut apart: how many, the server's sentence and where they are.

CancelDeletionRequest.description:
The same credentials as signing in: `Email` and `Password`, or `Provider` and `IdToken` (with `Nonce` when the app
used one). They are what proves who is cancelling; nothing else in the body is trusted.

CategoryCount.description: `Slug` is the item's own (leaf) category slug; null counts the items without a category.

CloseDayResponse.description:
`ClosedNow`: this call closed the day (false: it was closed before and nothing changed). The rest is the day's row: when it closed, the
ranked human outfits (the N of the percentile), the engine outfits, the counted votes in the fit, the Bradley–Terry iterations and whether
they converged, and how long the close took.

ConsentResponse.description: The current posting consent and, when the caller accepted this version, when.

CostPerWearItem.description: A most-worn piece with its price. `PriceIsEstimate` is true when the price is the catalog's (the app says "tahmini").

CreatePersonaRequest.description: Every field but the name and icon is optional. Seasons default to all four, formality to 1-5.

CreatePostUploadUrlResponse.description: PUT the photo to `UploadUrl` with exactly `Headers` before `ExpiresAt`, then call `process`.

CreateUploadUrlResponse.description: PUT the photo to `UploadUrl` with exactly `Headers` before `ExpiresAt`, then call `process`.

CreatorPageResponse.description: A creator's public page: the profile, the disclosure line to show, and their first page of posts the caller may see.

CreatorStatsResponse.description:
The owner's numbers over the last `Days`. `EstimatedEarnings` is an estimate (its inputs are listed); `ConfirmedEarnings`
sums imported conversions, 0 until the import exists.

DailyOutfitResponse.description:
`Outfit` is null only when nothing wearable could be built (then `Message` says so). `WardrobeEmpty` means the outfits
are catalog shopping ideas (`kind` Shopping, `completeness` CatalogOnly). `Weather` is the forecast used, if any.

DeleteAccountRequest.description: `Password` is required for an account that has one; `Confirm` is the word "SİL" (any casing).

DeleteAccountResponse.description: `DeletionScheduledFor` is the date the data will be gone; signing in again before it offers to cancel.

EarningsEstimate.description: An estimate of what a creator earned from clicks, with every input shown so the app can say how it was computed.

EventItem.description:
One event as the app sends it. `AnonymousId` is the device's pre-login ID; it is required while the caller is anonymous and
recommended after login. `Properties` is a flat object whose keys depend on `Name` (AnalyticsEventCatalog).

ExternalSignInRequest.description:
An ID token the app obtained from Google or Apple on the device. `DisplayName` is used only when this sign-in creates the account
(Apple gives the app the user's name once, on the very first sign-in). `Nonce` is the raw nonce the app generated for the provider,
when it used one. Nothing in the body is trusted for identity: who the user is comes from the verified token's claims alone.

FeedResponse.description: A page of 20 over at most ~230 ranked posts; `HasMore` says whether the next page has any.

HowToWearResponse.description:
`Outfits` are built around the anchor (in every outfit with `role` Anchor), wardrobe pieces first; gaps come from the catalog
within the persona's budget, each with its cheapest offer, and `completionPrice` sums them. A product the user already owns is
anchored as the wardrobe item. `Message` explains an empty list or catalog-only ideas.

JoinLeagueRequest.description: The consent version the player saw on the join screen; only the current one is accepted.

KnownSize.description: The size map's entry for the product's brand and group, so the app can pre-fill the answer. Absent when the user has none.

LeagueConsentResponse.description: The consent text the join screen shows, and its version (sent back by `POST /league/join`).

LeagueMeResponse.description:
The caller's league state. `Joined`: in the league now. `ConsentRequired`: the join screen must be shown (never joined, left, or
joined under an older consent version). `Tier` is null for someone who never joined; a player who left keeps theirs. `Today`: the
day's entry and votes. `Week`: the caller's group this week (null when not in one).

LeaguePairResponse.description:
`Id`: random per serve, the only identifier the voter sees. `Sequence`: 1 to the day's limit (a number is never reused,
    even when the pair it named was deleted with an account).

LeaguePieceResponse.description:
One piece of an outfit as the league shows it: the slot and an image, nothing else. To a voter the image is always the league's own copy
(a random key, new every day) or a catalog image. The league's promise is no name, no profile and no stable identifier in any response; it is
not that an outfit cannot be traced to its owner, because the picture is the owner's own photo (only the file's bytes differ) and someone who
knows the piece can recognise it. `ImageUrl` is null only in the owner's own view of an entry whose piece has no image any more.

LeaguePointsResponse.description:
The day's points: from the votes (0-70), voting on ten pairs (0/15), the worn outfit (0/10), a piece added (0/5), and the total shown.
While the outfit is under review `Votes` is null and `Total` is the usage points only.

LeagueResultEntryResponse.description: The caller's own outfit of that day, as the owner sees it.

LeagueResultsResponse.description:
The caller's result of one closed day (screen 04, "Akşamki sonuç"). `Status` and `Message`: LeagueResultStatus;
the message is "Kombinin inceleniyor. Sonuç inceleme bitince görünecek." while under review, the removal's line (`LeagueCopy.Removed`)
when a review took the outfit out, null for a final result. `Entry`: their own outfit
(null when they had none, or it is older than the entries are kept). `Competed`: it was in the pool at the close. `Ranked`: it
reached the comparisons to be ranked (null while under review); when false the app says "yeterli oy toplanamadı". `Rank` (1 = best) of `RankedCount` ranked outfits; `Comparisons`: the counted
votes on it. `PiecePointsAvailable`: a piece added now would still earn its points this week ("Eklersen 5 puan"). Nothing about any
other player.

LeagueResultStatus.description:
`Final`: the result as the close decided it. `UnderReview`: the outfit was reported and waits for a review; the rank and the vote
points are held back (they are stored and already count in the week). `Removed`: a review took the outfit out after the close; it has
no rank and no vote points.

LeagueResultsWeekResponse.description: The caller's week of that day (their tier, place in the group, points to the promotion line, when it ends); null when they were in no group.

LeagueReviewItem.description:
One reported outfit waiting for a review: its entry ID (operators only; never shown to players), its day and status, the reports that count
toward the hide and every report since the last review, whether a closed day's result is held back for it (`UnderReview`), and the pieces
as voters see them.

LeagueSideResponse.description: One side of a pair: the outfit's pieces as slot and image, nothing else (no entry ID, no owner, no occasion or audience label).

LeagueTableResponse.description:
The caller's group table this week (screen 05, "Haftalık lig"). `Tier`: the caller's own league this week; `TierUp` /
`TierDown`: the leagues above and below it (null at Diamond / Bronze). `TodayPoints`: today's total once today is closed
(`TodayIsFinal`), else the usage points earned so far today. `PromoteCount` / `RelegateCount`: the bands as they stand
(`min(5, floor(competed / 3))`). `Rows`: `{ rank, points, isMe, alias }` in table order, nothing else; the app shows "Sen" for
`isMe`. `State`: Open (the week runs), Ending (the week is over but its close has not run, so the next groups are not formed: this is
last week's table as the day closes left it, at any hour of Sunday evening or Monday if the close is late) or Final (closed: between
Sunday's close and Monday 00:00 it is last week's final table).

LeagueTableRow.description: One row of a group table as everyone in the group sees it: the place, the week points, whether it is the caller, the week's alias.

LeagueTodayEntryResponse.description:
The caller's outfit in today's league. `Status`: Pending (waiting for the image safety check), Competing, NotCompeting (with a
`Reason`), Withdrawn, Removed. `Message` is the Turkish line to show (`LeagueCopy`): one for every `Reason` of a NotCompeting entry
(RecentlyCompeted, UnsafePiece, IncompleteOutfit, PieceUnavailable, AgeRestricted, NotWorn) and one for Removed; null for Pending, Competing
and Withdrawn. The pieces are the owner's own view.

LeagueTodayResponse.description:
Today in the league (an Istanbul day). `ClosesAt`: votes stop and the results come (21:00 Istanbul). `Entry`: the caller's outfit,
null when no worn outfit entered. `ServedPairs` / `CountedVotes`: the caller's pairs today and the votes that counted; `Target`
counted votes earn the voting points, `Limit` pairs is the day's cap.

LeagueWeekResponse.description:
The caller's week in their group: place, group size, week points so far (the best five closed days), points to the promotion line ("5. sıraya
17 puan"; null inside the band or without one) and when the week ends. `State`: Open (running), Ending (the week is over and its close has
not run yet: this is last week's table until the new groups are formed, never an error) or Final (closed). Null for a player in no group.

LeagueWeekState.description:
Where a week stands: `Open` (it is running), `Ending` (its last close has passed but the week close has not run: the table is as the day
closes left it, and the next week's groups are still to be formed) or `Final` (closed: the stored final table).

LegalResponse.description: What the app needs to link to the legal texts and to know when to ask users to read them again.

LensBox.description: Fractions of the photo (0-1): left, top, width, height.

LensOfferResponse.description: The product's cheapest sellable offer by effective price. `GoPath` (`src=lens`) is the only way to open it.

LensRegionResponse.description:
A garment found in the photo. `Category`, `Slot`, `Family` and `Color` are null for the whole-photo region (nothing was
detected). `FamilyRestricted` is false when the search was widened (low confidence) or covered every family. An empty
`Results` is an honest "no close product". `WardrobeMatches` is present only for a signed-in caller.

LensResultResponse.description:
One catalog match. `Product` is the catalog list item. `Similarity` (0-1) is for analytics buckets and ordering; the app shows
`Level` (`close` "yakın eşleşme", `similar` "benzer"), never a percentage. `Offer` is null when nothing can be bought now.

LensSearchResponse.description:
Regions with results come first (best match first), then the empty ones, so the app can select the first. `Audience` is the filter
that was applied (null: none); `WholePhoto` is true when no garment region was found and the photo was searched as a whole.

LensWardrobeMatchResponse.description: One of the caller's own pieces close to the region: `exact` or `similar`, as in Social.

LoginRequest.description: `AnonymousId` is the analytics ID the app used before login; its earlier events are attached to the user.

LogoutRequest.description: `ExpoPushToken` is the phone's push token; when given, that device stops receiving pushes for this account.

NotificationResponse.description: `Status` tells the app whether the push went out; the feed shows `Pending`, `Sent` and `Suppressed` alike.

OfferResponse.description:
`GoPath` (`/api/v1/go/{offerId}`) is the only way to open an offer: the redirect records the click and adds the affiliate
parameters. The seller's own URL is never part of the response.

OutfitCompleteness.description: How much of the outfit the user already owns. Honesty about gaps is part of the contract with the app.

OutfitFeedbackRequest.description:
`Action`: Save, Dismiss, Worn or Shuffle. Save, Dismiss and Worn do what their own endpoints do; Shuffle ("another one") is only
recorded. `Reason` is for Dismiss only (default Other).

OutfitOfferResponse.description: A catalog piece's cheapest offer when it was suggested. `GoPath` is the only way to open it (the click is recorded).

OutfitPieceResponse.description:
One piece. A wardrobe piece has `WardrobeItemId` and its thumbnail; a catalog piece (`Role` Gap, or an Anchor from the
catalog) has `ProductId`, the product image and `Offer`.

OutfitResponse.description:
An outfit. `CompletionPrice` is what the gap pieces cost (their cheapest offers, effective price), null when there are none;
`AnchorPrice` is the catalog anchor's price; `TotalPrice` both together. `Rule` names why it works.

OutfitWeatherResponse.description: The forecast the outfit was built for. `TemperatureC` is the day's dressing temperature, `(2·max + min) / 3`.

PairingCompanion.description: A piece that goes with the item. `Score` is 0-100 (see `OutfitPairs`), `Reason` names the colour harmony.

PairingSlot.description: A slot other than the item's own, possibly empty. `Total` counts every companion in it, also those past the limit.

PairingsResponse.description:
What goes with one wardrobe item. `PersonaId` is the persona the scores are weighted for, or null for a user without personas.
`OutfitCount` is how many of the outfits behind the stats' `possibleOutfits` wear the item; a layer or an accessory counts the
outfits it can be worn with. `Unlock` is null when every slot has enough companions, or the catalog has nothing that fits.

PairingUnlock.description:
The catalog piece that would help the item most. `LowestPrice`, `CheapestSeller` and `GoPath` are one offer, the cheapest
by effective price. `UnlocksEstimate` is the outfits the item would gain. `MatchScore` is present only with a persona.

PairReason.description: Why two pieces go together, in the word clients read.

PostAuthorResponse.description: `Handle` and `IsCreator` come from the creator profile; other users have only a display name.

PostImageResponse.description: Private objects behind presigned GETs valid for an hour: cache them by post ID, not by URL. `Aspect` is width / height.

PostKind.description: A photo of someone in an outfit, or a saved outfit shown as a collage of its pieces (no person).

PostProposalResponse.description: An unconfirmed proposal (the detector's guess or an outfit piece), shown to the author only, in the tag editor.

PostResponse.description:
A post as the caller may see it. `Image` is null for an outfit post (lay the tags' images out as a collage) and before processing.
`MatchScore` is the viewer's persona match of the product tags. `Disclosure` is set on creators' posts and must be shown.
`StatusMessage` and `Proposals` are for the author only. `Reason` appears in the feed.

PostStatus.description:
`Processing` → `Blocked` | `NeedsReview` | `Draft` (or `Failed` when the photo could not be processed); the
author's confirmation turns a `Draft` into `Live` (a `NeedsReview` post waits for a reviewer). Three reports hide a
`Live` post. `Deleted` is a tombstone until the purge job.

PostSummaryResponse.description: The band under the photo: "Bu kombin toplam `TotalPrice` ₺ · `PieceCount` parça · `OwnedCount`'si dolabında var".

PostTagResponse.description:
A confirmed tag. `InWardrobe` is the viewer's: `exact` (they own that product, or it is their own piece), `similar` (they own a
ready piece of the same category and colour), null otherwise or when signed out. `ImageUrl` of a wardrobe tag is null for anyone but
the piece's owner until the safety filter allowed that photo.

PostTagSource.description: Where a tag came from. Whatever the source, a tag is shown to viewers only once the author confirmed it.

PostVisibility.description: Who may see a live post. New posts are PostVisibility.Private until the author chooses otherwise.

PreferencesResponse.description: What the preference endpoints return. Quiet hours are `HH:mm` local times in string PreferencesResponse.TimeZone.

PriceSummary.description: Computed over in-stock prices only: the lowest of the active offers now, and the extremes seen in snapshots.

ProductListItem.description: Prices and `CheapestSeller` are those of the product's lowest active, in-stock offer. `MatchScore` (0-100) is present only when the request named a persona.

ProductResponse.description: `MatchScore` is present when the request named a persona; `SizeHint` when the caller is signed in. Both are left out otherwise.

ProductSummary.description: The few product fields every engagement list shows next to its own data. `LowestPrice` is null when nothing can be bought.

PublishPostRequest.description:
`Visibility` is `Private`, `Followers` or `Public`. `Followers` is not private: anyone signed in can follow without
approval and then sees the post (security review M5). `Tags` replaces every tag and proposal of the post.

PublishTag.description:
One confirmed tag. `Kind` is `Wardrobe` (with one of the author's `WardrobeItemId`), `Product` (with a
`ProductId`) or `Unknown` (an optional `Label`). The box is fractions of the image (clamped into it).

PushDelivery.description: What Expo said about one message (one notification to one device). `Status` is `ok`, `error` or `unreachable`.

PutCreatorRequest.description: `Handle` 3-30 of a-z, 0-9, `.` and `_` (lower-cased); `IsActive` defaults to true. Every field is replaced.

PutSellerRequest.description:
The seller. `Name`, `Kind`, `WebsiteUrl` and `IsActive` are replaced on every PUT. The affiliate fields are the
exception, because workers that only know the shop would otherwise wipe what was configured by hand: left out = unchanged, an explicit
null (or blank) = cleared. The `*Set` flags record which of them the body contained; the JSON reader only calls an init accessor
for a property that is present.

RecordWearRequest.description: `WornOn` defaults to today in Europe/Istanbul. The body may be left out entirely.

RegisterRequest.description: `AnonymousId` is the analytics ID the app used before registering; its earlier events are attached to the new user.

ReportEntryRequest.description: `Side`: `left` or `right`, the outfit of the pair being reported. `Reason`: Inappropriate, NotClothing or Other (optional).

ReportPostRequest.description: `Reason`: Nudity, Violence, Hate, Harassment, Spam, Scam or Other.

ReportTryOnRequest.description:
"Yanlış görünüyor": exactly one of `OutfitId` and `ProductId` (what `GET /me/tryon` was asked with), the `GarmentIds` of
its answer (the pieces' IDs, every one of them in the drawing) and the `Renderer` that drew it (`renderer` of the Ready answer).

ReviewEntryRequest.description: `Decision`: `Restore` (clear the reports, show a held-back result) or `Remove` (take the outfit out for good), any casing.

ReviewEntryResponse.description: The entry's status after the review, and whether a closed day's result changed with it.

ReviewItem.description: A post waiting for a human: why (moderation labels or reports), and a 1-hour link to its preview.

ReviewPostRequest.description:
`Decision`: `Approve`, `Remove` or `Keep` (leave it as it is, at the back of the queue). `Reason` is what the
author reads when the post is removed (at most 200 characters; the standard copy when left out).

RunEmbeddingsRequest.description: `Limit`: how many due products to work on (default 100, at most 1000); `ProductIds` restricts the run to those products.

SavedProductItem.description:
The catalog's ProductListItem fields, flattened, plus `isActive` (saved products stay in the list after they
are delisted) and `savedAt`. A product nobody sells has `offerCount` 0 and `lowestPrice` 0.

SaveTripRequest.description: `Name` (1-60 characters) and the plan request (`POST /me/trips/plan`'s body).

SellerRef.description: The seller of the offer that defines `lowestPrice`, for the "from X" label next to the price.

SendTestResponse.description: The notification as the push sender left it, and what Expo said about each device it was sent to.

SizeHintResponse.description:
Which size to buy. `Size`, `Source` and `Confidence` are the user's own entry for the product's brand and group, when
there is one. Without it `Suggestion` may carry a guess from the user's sizes at other brands (not stored).

SizePromptAnswer.description: How the user answered "Aldın mı? Beden uydu mu?".

SizePromptResponse.description:
One open question. `Group` is the size group the answer will be stored under; `AvailableSizes` are the sizes the clicked offer
listed (possibly none); `ExpiresAt` is when the question goes away by itself.

SizeSuggestion.description: A guess, not stored anywhere: what the user probably wears at a brand they have not told us about.

StoredAnalysis.description: What is kept of a vision answer in `AnalysisJson`: everything except the images and the embedding (stored on their own).

StyleCardsResponse.description: `Remaining` counts the unswiped cards that did not fit into this response.

StyleFamily.description: The broad style families a style card (and, heuristically, a product) belongs to.

StyleResponse.description: The whole derived style profile, weights included. For debugging and the app's "tarzın" screen.

StyleSummary.description: What the app shows about a persona's learned taste. `TopColors` has up to 3 names, `TopFamilies` up to 2.

SubmitSwipesResponse.description: `OnboardingCompleted` turns true once any persona has reached int SubmitSwipesEndpoint.OnboardingLikes likes.

SweepOffersRequest.description: The body is optional; without a seller the whole catalog is swept.

TagOfferResponse.description: The product's current cheapest sellable offer (effective price). `GoPath` is the only way to open it; it records the click for the post.

TriggerResponse.description: `AlertId` is null once the alert has been deleted.

TripGapReason.description: Why a day of a trip has no outfit, as far as one slot is concerned.

TripGapResponse.description: `Days` are the trip days the piece would dress. `Suggestion` is one catalog piece for it (a `goPath` with `src=trip`).

TripOccasionRequest.description: A plan for one day of the trip: `Occasion` is office, weekend, evening, sport or event.

TripPackGroup.description: The packing list of one slot.

TripPlanRequest.description:
"Valiz hazırlama": the destination `City`, `StartDate`..`EndDate` (1-14 days, from today up to a year ahead), optional plans per day,
at most `MaxPieces` packed (3-60), shoes on consecutive days (`AllowRepeatShoes`, default true), laundry on the way (`Laundry`,
default false). `PersonaId` follows the catalog convention.

TripPlanResponse.description:
A packing plan. `Pieces` is the packing list grouped by slot, each piece with the number of days it is worn; `Days` one entry per day
with its weather and outfit (null when none could be made); `Coverage` the days with an outfit; `Gaps` what is missing and why.
A piece removed from the wardrobe since the plan was made is `Missing`.

TripResponse.description: A saved trip: its name, what was asked, when it was last planned, and the plan.

TripWeatherResponse.description:
The day's weather and where it came from: `Forecast` (Open-Meteo, within 16 days), `Normal` (the climate normals of that calendar day)
or `Season` (neither; the temperatures are then null and `Season` decided).

TryGroup.description:
The outfits built around one tagged product. `Owned`: the caller already has it, so the anchor is their own piece. The anchor's offer
keeps the post attribution (`goPath` with `post=`); gap pieces carry their own cheapest offer.

TryOnGarmentResponse.description: One piece of a drawing: `Id` is the piece's ID as the outfit carries it (wardrobe item or product).

TryOnResponse.description:
"Manken üstünde gör". `Status`: `Ready` (show `ImageUrl`, a presigned GET valid for an hour, with "Manken üzerinde yaklaşık
görünüm"), `Preparing` (show "Hazırlanıyor" and ask again), `Unavailable` (hide the action entirely, never a disabled button).
`Garments` (Ready only): each drawn piece by the ID the outfit gives it (wardrobe item or product) with its fit label, null when nothing
was comparable. `DefaultedMeasurements` (Ready only): the measurements the mannequin guessed; not empty → "Ölçülerini ekle, manken sana
benzesin". `Reason` (Unavailable only): why, for the app team and support. `Renderer` (Ready with an image only): the name of the
renderer that drew it, sent back as `renderer` of `POST /me/tryon/reports` ("Yanlış görünüyor"); null otherwise, a check included.

TryOnStatus.description: What the app does: show the image, show "Hazırlanıyor", or hide the action entirely.

TryWithWardrobeRequest.description: All optional: `Seed` re-ranks near-equal outfits, `Occasion` and `PersonaId` as on how-to-wear.

UnwornItem.description: A piece of "Giymediklerin". `Reason` is the likely one (null when none); `Unlock` is the pairings route's catalog suggestion, present for the first few "eşi yok" pieces only.

UnwornSection.description: `TotalCount` counts every such piece, `Items` are the oldest int WardrobeSummaryRules.UnwornListLimit of them.

UpdateAlertRequest.description: A partial update: a null field is left as it is. `Sizes: []` clears the size filter.

UpdateItemRequest.description:
A partial update: a null field is left as it is, and `Clear` names the optional fields to empty (IReadOnlyList<string> UpdateItemRequest.ClearableFields).
An empty body is valid: it is the one-tap "looks right" confirmation. Enum values are names, matched case-insensitively.

UpdatePersonaRequest.description:
A partial update: a null field is left as it is, and a given list replaces the stored one (`[]` clears preferred/avoided
lists, but not seasons). `ClearBudget: true` removes both budget bounds.

UpdatePreferencesRequest.description:
A partial update: a null field is left as it is. Quiet hours are `HH:mm` local times in Europe/Istanbul and come as a pair;
`ClearQuietHours: true` removes them.

UpdateProfileRequest.description:
The measurements and the city, the same way as the seller PUT: left out = unchanged, an explicit null = cleared. The `*Set` flags
record which of them the body contained; the JSON reader only calls an init accessor for a property that is present. `Audience` is
the exception, a null keeps the current one too (a profile always has an audience), and so is `SizePromptsEnabled` ("beden sorularını kapat":
false stops the "did the size fit?" questions, a flag is never cleared). `City` (at most 80 characters; blank clears it)
is where the outfit engine reads the weather.

UpsertItemResult.description: An item that was stored: the IDs let a worker reconcile its own records with ours.

UserProfileResponse.description:
A user as others see them. `Handle`, `Bio` and `Link` exist for creators only. `PostCount` counts the posts the caller
may see. `IsFollowing`: the caller follows them; `FollowsYou`: they follow the caller.

VisionColor.description: `Name` is a `ProductColor` name; `Hex` the measured shade.

VoteRequest.description: `Choice`: `left`, `right` or `skip` ("Karar veremedim"), any casing. `DecisionMs`: what the app measured from display to tap.

VoteResponse.description:
`Counted`: the vote counts (not a skip, not too fast). `ChosenWinRate` (0-100) and `ChosenGames`: the chosen outfit's real record
today, this vote included; the rate is null below `League:MinGamesForWinRate` games ("İlk oylardan biri seninki"), both are null for a
skip. The rest is the voter's progress: counted votes and served pairs today, the target for the voting points and the day's limit.

WardrobeGap.description: `CategorySlug` is the top-level category of the missing piece (`ust-giyim`, ...).

WardrobeGapsResponse.description:
`PersonaId` is the persona the analysis was made for (the active one, else the first), or null for a user without personas.
`SuggestedProducts` fill the first gap: catalog items of its category, color and formality band, active and in stock, not
already in the wardrobe, and with a persona a `matchScore` of at least int GetGapsEndpoint.MinMatchScore.

WardrobeItemResponse.description:
One wardrobe item. `ThumbUrl`/`CutoutUrl` are public and permanent (a catalog item whose image could not be copied shows the
catalog's image); `OriginalUrl` is a 15-minute presigned link, given only when there is no cutout to show. `NeedsCategory`
asks the app to let the user pick one of `Analysis.CategoryCandidates`. `Analysis` is there once a photo was analysed.

WardrobeItemSummary.description:
An item in lists (the wardrobe grid, the stats' most and least worn). `CompanionCount`, how many pieces of the wardrobe it pairs
with, is present only on `GET /items`; an item that cannot be worn (yet) has 0.

WardrobeStatsResponse.description:
Over the wardrobe (not archived, not failed). An item counts as unworn for 180 days when its last wear, or its creation when it was
never worn, is more than 180 days ago. `PossibleOutfits` is the outfit engine's count of complete, wearable core outfits (top,
bottom, shoes) the wardrobe makes, capped at 999 (see `OutfitCounter`); never null since Task 12. `UnmatchedCount` is how many
wearable pieces pair with nothing else in the wardrobe (`companionCount` 0 on the grid): the pieces a purchase would unlock.

WardrobeSummaryResponse.description:
The wardrobe summary. With too few pieces only `PieceCount` and `Message` are there: no totals, no zeros that look like data.
Otherwise `Value`, `CostPerWear` and `Unworn` are (see WardrobeSummaryRules). Every price that is not the
user's own is marked: `Value.IsEstimate`, `CategoryValue.IsEstimate`, `CostPerWearItem.PriceIsEstimate`.

WardrobeValue.description:
The wardrobe's value. `Total` is `KnownTotal` (own prices) plus `EstimatedTotal` (catalog prices of linked pieces), null when
no piece has a price. `IsEstimate` says the total includes estimates: the app labels it "tahmini". `Counts` are disjoint and add
up to the number of pieces.

WearResponse.description: `WornOn` is the day just recorded, or null after an undo.

WeatherSource.description: Where a day's weather came from: the forecast, the climate normals of that calendar day, or nothing (the season decides).
